findings.title: Server-recipient mode: the pinned operational key is an authorised author, so a compromised authoritative node can still forge any ACL change replicas accept
findings.detail: Step 13 admits `author in admins(head.acl) UNION head.pinned`; step 14 lets a pinned author un-pin others; step 15 exempts pinned authors from the last-admin rule. In server-recipient mode (the recommended drop-in default) the server's operational Ed25519 key is pinned in every epoch and is online on the same host as the endpoint key and the store. An attacker who owns the authoritative node signs an epoch that removes every admin, un-pins the backup key, adds itself as sole admin-reader and rotates; replicas verify it as valid and the operator renders whatever the attacker encrypts. Section 12.4 nevertheless claims this mode gains 'a compromised authoritative node can no longer forge ACL changes that replicas accept'. Only attribution survives; the replica-side gain is E2E-only.
findings.fix: Separate recipient from authority. Give pinned entries a role (`pinned: [[bstr id, uint role]]`, recipient-only vs recovery). Steps 13/14/15 authorise only admins(head.acl) and recovery-pinned keys. Let the operational key author only shrink-or-rotate epochs: verifier rule 'if author is recipient-only pinned then acl <= head.acl entrywise (no new rows, no raised bits) and pinned == head.pinned'. Grant-revoke, RotateDek and RemoveIdentity keep working server-side while a compromised node degrades to denial. State in 12.4 which gains hold per mode.

findings.title: A Put racing a rotation lands under the pruned generation and becomes undecryptable by everyone; the upload is never checked for coverage
findings.detail: SubmitEpoch's CAS covers only (group_id, head_epoch). `Bunker::put` (src/server.rs) encrypts under `store.current_dek_version` = MAX(group_dek.version) and inserts a secret_version row. A Put between the admin's download and the commit (any writer in server-recipient mode, any recipient in E2E) still passes the CAS; the epoch commits, old wrap sets are pruned, and the new row references a dek_version nobody can open (in E2E not even the server) while the writer received Version{n}. Step 9 only requires the `reencrypted` digest to match 'the uploaded set', never that the set equals the group's secret_version rows, so an author can omit versions (bricking them on prune) or add phantom rows the signature vouches for.
findings.fix: Inside the commit transaction: (a) assert the uploaded set equals `SELECT name, version FROM secret JOIN secret_version` for the group (count + set equality) else EpochConflict; (b) fence writes with a `rotation_pending(group_id, epoch_hash, started_at)` row that makes Put/Delete answer VersionConflict/Failed between BeginRotation and commit/abort, or add a per-group `write_seq` bumped by put_secret/delete_secret to the CAS tuple; (c) make `put` refuse to encrypt under a dek_version older than the head epoch's.

findings.title: Client-side re-encryption of 'every retained version' has no download path and cannot fit the 4 MiB request cap
findings.detail: Every read of secret_version in src/store.rs joins on `s.current_version` (secret_current, secret_entries, secret_data_current, read_secret); no Request variant returns ciphertext, a nonce, or a non-current version, and `Get` returns plaintext only. Sync carries ciphertext but only current versions and only to explicit readers. So an admin cannot obtain the history it is told to re-encrypt. `SubmitEpoch { group, record, versions }` 'in one request' must fit proto::MAX_MSG = 4 MiB, yet one secret may be just under 4 MiB (why SYNC_MAX_MSG is 8 MiB); the 'staged upload' alternative names no requests, no pending table, no GC. secret_version retains every version forever, so nothing bounds the total.
findings.fix: Recommended (YAGNI): rotation re-encrypts the current version of each secret and deletes older versions in the same transaction (sync already mirrors current-only). Add `GetCiphertext { group, name }` -> `Ciphertext { version, dek_version, nonce, ciphertext }` (read-gated) and a per-stream `StageVersion { pending: epoch_hash, name, version, nonce, ciphertext }` into a `pending_version` table, then `SubmitEpoch { group, record }` moves staged rows in, checks coverage, commits; TTL-expire abandoned stages. If history must survive, add `version` to both requests and state the bandwidth cost with a number.

findings.title: The migration epoch fails the design's own step 7, and the Bunker has no access to the key it is told to sign with
findings.detail: 12.5 mints migrated groups' epoch 1 with `author = authoritative endpoint id`, `pinned = {backup, operational}`; 12.2 says the server checks epoch 1 with steps 1-9, 13, 15. Step 7 requires `author in readers(acl) UNION pinned` whenever key material moves, which epoch 1 always does. The endpoint key is deliberately distinct from the operational key and is not a registered identity, so it is in neither set: the server rejects the epoch it just minted. Also `Bunker::new(store, op_identity)` never receives the endpoint SecretKey; src/main.rs hands server.key only to bind_serve_endpoint.
findings.fix: Author migration epochs with the operational Ed25519 key (pinned, so steps 7 and 13 pass with no special case) and drop the replica-side `{authoritative endpoint id}` exception. Pass the operational Ed25519 signing key into Bunker::new alongside the age identity for the transition.

findings.title: Startup backfill refuses to start and `recover` silently skips migrated groups once dek_wrap rows are deleted
findings.detail: `Store::missing_reader_wraps` is `group_acl JOIN group_dek LEFT JOIN dek_wrap ... WHERE w.recipient IS NULL`. The design deletes a migrated group's dek_wrap rows but keeps group_dek (adding columns to it). Every (group, version, reader) of every epoch group is then 'missing'; `Bunker::backfill_reader_wraps` calls `unwrap_dek`, fails with 'no operational wrap', and main.rs propagates the error so `serve` never starts. `Recover` iterates `all_wraps_for_recipient('backup')`, finds nothing for epoch groups and reports success having re-keyed none of them.
findings.fix: Gate both on epoch presence (`AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM group_epoch e WHERE e.group_id = a.group_id)`); make `recover` error out, not skip, when group_epoch rows exist, and specify the offline epoch recovery: `db recover-epoch --backup-key --group` opens the backup wrap in the head, mints a pinned-set-change epoch to the new operational key, appends it locally with audit row `(local)/submit-epoch`. Add a test that opens a migrated DB and asserts backfill_reader_wraps() == 0 and serve boots.

findings.title: CreateGroup's reply cannot carry the pinned set without breaking the Go client, and client-minted genesis needs that set before the call
findings.detail: `Response::Ok` is a unit variant encoded as the bare string "Ok"; docs/protocol.md section 8 says an unknown response variant is an error and the Go client pins that. Turning CreateGroup's success into a struct variant breaks `secret-bunker/1`. Independently, 12.2 says epoch 1 is minted client-side and submitted with the creation using `pinned` 'delivered in the CreateGroup reply': the client needs the value one round-trip before it can exist.
findings.fix: Keep `CreateGroup { name }` -> `Ok` unchanged (server-minted genesis). Add additive variants: `GroupPolicy` -> `Policy { mode, pinned: [[id, role]] }` for any registered identity, and `CreateGroupWithEpoch { name, record: bytes }` -> `Ok | Failed`, service-admin gated. Add both to the proto golden vectors and protocol.md.

findings.title: 'Full chain on first sight, tail on Changed' is not expressible over the sync protocol, and an unchunked Group message dies at the frame cap
findings.detail: The push path is `Changed{group}` -> `FetchGroup{group}` -> full snapshot; the server keeps no per-session cursor and FetchGroup has no `since`, so it cannot know which epochs the replica holds. Sending the whole chain each time grows ~75 B x recipients per epoch; docs/sync-protocol.md documents that `Group` is not chunked and a Group over SYNC_MAX_MSG kills the stream and every reconnect 'fails identically' - a 1000-reader group wedges every replica after roughly 100 epochs. `GetEpochs` lives only on the client ALPN, which replicas do not use.
findings.fix: Add `epochs_since: Option<u64>` to `FetchGroup` (additive; an old server ignores it) and define `Group.epochs` as records with epoch > epochs_since, head always included; extend the Group merge rule to append `epochs` and chunk them byte-budgeted. For the manifest add a struct `Hello { known: [[group, head_epoch]] }` next to the unit `Hello`.

findings.title: The replica cannot derive its ACL from the verified head: identity names are outside the body but the mirror's schema and API require them
findings.detail: 12.5 says the replica derives ACL and its own wrap from the head and that `acl`/`deks` become optional, while 2.1 keeps identity names out of the body. On the replica `identity.name` is NOT NULL UNIQUE, `apply_group_sync` rule 1 keys the stale-name delete on `identity_name`, `GroupAcl`/`ListIdentityNames` answer names, and `created_by` is a name. Without `acl` the replica cannot apply the state.
findings.fix: Keep `acl` mandatory as the name map. Replica rule: the multiset {(endpoint_id, perms)} of the received `acl` must equal the verified head's `acl`, else reject the state fail-safe. Document that names remain trusted transport metadata.

findings.title: Mixed-version rollout silently stalls old replicas and operator pods on migrated groups
findings.detail: `DekEntry.wrapped` is an age file; `Replica::get` and `server::read_secret` open it with `crypto::unwrap_dek`. Once a group is on the epoch path the authoritative node has no age wrap to send (in E2E it cannot mint one), so an old replica/operator applying that group's `Group` sees every dek_version without a wrap, `apply_group_state` filters the secrets out (`skipped_undecryptable`), re-fetches once and leaves the group short. The operator maps that to `NotYetSynced` and keeps the last rendered k8s Secret forever with no error. 'acl/deks stay populated for one release' cannot be honoured for these groups.
findings.fix: Make the order normative: upgrade every replica and operator before `db migrate-epochs`; add a struct `Hello { epochs: true }` next to the unit `Hello` so the server can refuse (SyncDenied + warn) peers without epoch capability. In server-recipient mode optionally keep emitting age `deks` for one release; say explicitly that E2E groups have no compatibility path.

findings.title: E2E-mode RemoveIdentity leaves the removed identity authorised on every replica until an admin-reader acts
findings.detail: Today `remove_identity_with_rotations` deletes the row and the next sync shrinks the ACL immediately. In the design's E2E mode RemoveIdentity only removes the row and marks 'rotation pending'; the head epoch, from which replicas now derive authorisation, still lists the identity as reader with a wrap. Step 3 forbids the server an ACL-only epoch without that recipient (recipients must equal readers UNION pinned exactly, and the server cannot build a wrap set without M). The kicked key keeps read on every replica and the operator keeps rendering for it, indefinitely without an admin-reader - worse than today.
findings.fix: Allow a server-signed tombstone epoch: dek_version unchanged, wraps carried verbatim, ACL shrunk; verifier rule `readers(acl) UNION pinned SUBSET recipients(wraps)` with every surplus recipient a reader of head.acl absent from this acl. Replicas enforce the shrunk ACL at once; 'rotation pending' becomes the derived property 'head has surplus recipients' and the next admin-reader epoch must re-key. Pairs with finding 1's shrink-only server authority.

findings.title: Per-request full verification and whole-group re-encryption run under the single store mutex
findings.detail: `Bunker::handle` holds `store: Mutex<Store>` for the whole request and sync snapshots take the same lock. Section 6 step 1 ('never open an unverified record') per Get/Put means 2n+1 torsion checks plus n multiscalar muls per request (~15 ms at n = 100 by the design's own estimate) versus one X25519 unwrap today, blocking every client and sync session. `RemoveIdentity` in server-recipient mode must also re-encrypt every retained version of every readable group inside the one transaction the design keeps - O(total ciphertext bytes) under the lock instead of O(readers).
findings.fix: Verify at commit (SubmitEpoch/migration) and at load; cache `(group_id, epoch_hash) -> verified head` and `(group_id, dek_version) -> Zeroizing<Dek>` in Inner and serve Get/Put from it. For RemoveIdentity keep the row delete + tombstone epochs atomic and do re-encryption per group in follow-up transactions, or adopt current-versions-only rotation so cost is bounded by live size.

findings.title: Genesis trust is reset by the replica's own drop-and-re-add path; the body does not name the group
findings.detail: Replicas pin `hash(epoch 1)` per group, but the body carries only random `group_id` bytes, not the name, and the pin lives in the group's rows. src/replica.rs drops a group on `SyncDenied` (`drop_group_and_gc`) and on absence from a completed manifest, then re-creates it from scratch on the next manifest. A compromised authoritative node denies FetchGroup once, waits for the drop, and re-serves the same name with a fresh self-authored genesis (TOFU per 12.2) - exactly the forgery the design says replicas now resist. The AAD binds the group name, not group_id, so nothing ties the two.
findings.fix: Add `"group": tstr` to EpochBody and verify it equals `Group.name`. Persist the genesis pin per group name in `meta` or a `group_pin(name, genesis_hash)` table that survives `drop_group_local`; reject and log a different genesis for a known name until an operator clears the pin.

findings.title: Stricter last-admin rule breaks migration of groups whose only admin lacks read, and changes Grant behaviour
findings.detail: Today's guard is `admin_count >= 1`; an identity may hold `a` without `r` (`parse_perms("a")` is legal; `grant_cannot_drop_the_last_group_admin` protects only the admin bit). Step 15 requires an admin who is also a reader unless the author is pinned. A migrated group whose sole admin is write/admin-only fails step 15 in its epoch 1 unless finding 4's fix is taken, and post-migration server-recipient `Grant` refuses edits that succeed today.
findings.fix: Add a migration pre-check that lists groups with no admin-reader and refuses to migrate them until fixed (`db grant ... rwa`); document the rule change under Grant in protocol.md. Alternatively apply step 15 only from epoch 2.

findings.title: New request/response variants are under-specified for the exhaustive matches, audit vocabulary, and E2E ciphertext paths
findings.detail: `Request::op()`/`target()`, `Bunker::touched_groups` and `ReplicaServer::dispatch` are deliberately exhaustive; the design names `SubmitEpoch`/`GetEpochs` but not their audit op/target, whether SubmitEpoch publishes on the event channel (it must, or replicas never see the rotation), or how a replica answers them. E2E mode says `Put` must carry ciphertext and loses plaintext `Get`, but gives no variants; overloading `Put.value`/`Secret.value` changes field semantics on the existing contract.
findings.fix: Specify audit rows `submit-epoch` (target `group@epoch:hexhash`) and `get-epochs`; add SubmitEpoch and CreateGroupWithEpoch to touched_groups; replica dispatch: SubmitEpoch -> ReadOnlyReplica, GetEpochs served from the mirror. Add `PutCiphertext { group, name, dek_version, nonce, ciphertext, expected_version }` and `GetCiphertext { group, name }` -> `Ciphertext { ... }` as new variants; in E2E mode plain Get/Put answer `Failed { reason }` after authorisation.

findings.title: Torsion validation must move to AddIdentity/db grant; subtle needs to be a direct dependency
findings.detail: Confirmed in ed25519-dalek 3.0.0: `VerifyingKey::from_bytes` only decompresses (no canonical or torsion check) and iroh's `PublicKey::from_bytes` calls it, so `Bunker::add_identity`'s `parse::<iroh::EndpointId>()` accepts a torsion-carrying or non-canonical key. Such an identity registers, can be granted write, and every later read grant or epoch touching it fails at verification with no attribution to the registration. `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` is used but subtle 2.6.1 is only transitive.
findings.fix: Run `decode_point` (recompress + is_torsion_free) in `add_identity` and `db_grant`, answering `Failed { reason: "invalid endpoint id" }`, with a test using `A + EIGHT_TORSION[1]`. Add `subtle = "2"` next to `curve25519-dalek = "5"` and `hkdf = "0.12"`.

findings.title: Automatic migration on first `serve` rewrites every ciphertext row and forces every replica to refetch everything
findings.detail: 12.5 runs migration on first start of the new binary, re-encrypting every retained version, deleting dek_wrap rows and minting epochs, with no opt-in; today's startup work (`backfill_reader_wraps`) only adds rows. Re-encryption changes `(dek_version, nonce)` for every current secret, so the nonce change-discriminator makes every replica refetch every secret of every group at once after the upgrade through the reconnect loop.
findings.fix: Make migration explicit only (`db migrate-epochs [--group]`), one transaction per group, refusing to run while `serve` holds the file; `serve` logs the count of unmigrated groups. Any remaining startup work runs before the sync ALPN is mounted, like the backfill.

findings.title: The testing story stops at crypto vectors; the integration surface that changes is untested
findings.detail: Section 11 pins golden vectors and negative crypto cases but names no store, server, sync or CLI tests, although the repository's confidence lives in store.rs/server.rs unit tests and tests/e2e.rs (e.g. `a_revoked_readers_wrap_cannot_open_later_writes`, which must now assert old ciphertext is gone rather than that new writes use a new DEK).
findings.fix: Add: store-level SubmitEpoch CAS vs Put race; replica rejects an epoch from an unauthorised author served by a fake authoritative built like `stalled_authoritative` in tests/e2e.rs; migration of a v2 DB with several dek versions and history followed by `backfill_reader_wraps() == 0` and `recover` refusing; old-binary replica against a migrated group; CLI tests for `db migrate-epochs` and offline recovery epochs; proto/sync golden vectors for every new variant.

strengths: Every crate-level claim checked is true for the pinned versions: CompressedEdwardsY::decompress masks bit 255 and never rejects y >= p (so recompress-and-compare is required), EdwardsPoint::is_torsion_free is exactly l*P == O, MontgomeryPoint::to_edwards(sign) and Scalar::from_canonical_bytes -> CtOption exist, vartime_double_scalar_mul_basepoint / VartimeMultiscalarMul are present, and curve25519-dalek 5.0.0 is bound to digest 0.11 and rand_core 0.10 while the project pins sha2 0.10 / rand 0.8 (Cargo.lock has both digest 0.10.7 and 0.11.3). Steering implementers to from_bytes_mod_order_wide avoids a real trap.
Signing the exact received CBOR bytes and decoding strictly matches how src/proto.rs uses ciborium today (serde map order, no canonical mode) and spares the Go client a canonical encoder.
The secret AAD, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and crypto::Dek are untouched and dek_version keeps its meaning, so secret_version rows and decrypt_secret need no change beyond re-encryption.

Correctly identifies that hkdf 0.12 is already in the lockfile via age and that curve25519-dalek must become a direct dependency (ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 re-exports only curve25519_dalek::digest::Digest, not the crate).
The reader-side dek_commit check and the 'consistency, not correctness' framing are honest about what a keyless verifier can see and match the brief's split-view ask without overclaiming.
Compare-and-set on (group_id, head_epoch) with EpochConflict{head} is the right shape and mirrors the existing VersionConflict CAS style.
verdict: The cryptographic core (Edwards ElGamal with one batched Schnorr proof, strict decode_point, HKDF split into DEK and commitment, sign-the-received-bytes) is sound and its API claims check out against the vendored curve25519-dalek 5.0.0 / ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 sources. As an implementation plan for this repository it does not work as written. Three blocking gaps: (1) in server-recipient mode the pinned operational key is an authorised author under steps 13-15 and is online on the authoritative host, so the claimed replica-side gain against a compromised authoritative node is false in the recommended default mode; (2) SubmitEpoch's CAS covers only (group_id, head_epoch), so a Put racing the rotation is stored under the pruned generation and becomes undecryptable by everyone while the writer sees success, and the upload is never checked to cover the group's rows; (3) client-side re-encryption of every retained version has no data path (no request returns ciphertext or non-current versions) and the single-request upload cannot fit MAX_MSG = 4 MiB. Further concrete breakages: the migration epoch fails the design's own step 7, the startup backfill refuses to boot and `recover` silently skips migrated groups once dek_wrap rows are deleted, changing CreateGroup's `Ok` reply breaks the Go client and is circular with client-minted genesis, 'tail of the chain on Changed' cannot be expressed over the stateless FetchGroup while an unchunked Group dies at 8 MiB, the replica cannot derive its ACL from a body that omits identity names, and E2E RemoveIdentity leaves the kicked key authorised on replicas. Revise the authority model (recipient != author; the server may only shrink or rotate), add a write fence plus upload-coverage check to the rotation commit, and either add ciphertext download / staged upload requests or redefine rotation as current-versions-only; then re-plan storage, migration and recovery around the existing backfill and recover paths before implementation planning.
